messages:
matt: oncall-bot just fired 3 GPU ECC/Xid alerts in the last 12m from two different nodes in us-west-2. looks like the dcgm_exporter spiked; paging fatigue incoming. anyone else seeing similar bursts?

oncall-bot: [ALERT] DCGM_ECC_XID_BURST on gpu-node-23.us-west-2 (severity: page) — 3 triggers in 12m. link: https://ops.redwood.ai/alerts/3612345678

sara: yup saw it. pattern: small bursts (1-2 XIDs) across cards then quiet. not sure if these are driver noise or real ECC events.

lee: we've been getting more of these after the kernel backport last week. Could be noise amplification from newer dcgm exporter sampling.

matt: proposal: move from raw per-event alerting to windowed increase() + cardinality bucketing so we only page on sustained/clustered failures. example rule draft:
```yaml
- alert: DCGM_ECC_XID_CLUSTER
  expr: increase(dcgm_gpu_xid_errors_total{job="dcgm_exporter"}[10m]) > 5
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "Clustered GPU XID errors"
    runbook: "https://go/redwood/runbooks/gpu-xid"
```

maya: I like switching to increase(), but also add by (instance, card_index) grouping and a lower-severity per-card alert for single-card streaks. That prevents noisy global pages.

lee: +1. Also consider a short suppression window for transient single-sample spikes: use max_over_time or quantile_over_time to ignore single-sample blips. e.g. `max_over_time(dcgm_gpu_ecc_samples[2m]) > 0` combined with increase.

devops: We should also avoid high-cardinality label expansion. Recommend grouping on `instance` and `gpu_uuid` only, drop pod/container labels in the alert expr.

matt: ok. here's a slightly more concrete rule patch I'll put in a PR tomorrow:
```yaml
- alert: DCGM_XID_SUSTAINED
  expr: sum by (instance, gpu_uuid) (increase(dcgm_gpu_xid_errors_total{job="dcgm_exporter"}[15m])) >= 3
  for: 15m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "Sustained XID errors on a GPU"
    description: ">=3 XID errors in 15m on a single gpu_uuid. Suggest drain and hardware triage."
```

sara: can we also add a lower-priority alert for ephemeral spikes that populates a dashboard but doesn't page? e.g. severity: warning and no for: clause.

matt: yep — dashboard metric + warning alert. want to track regressions without waking oncall.

lee: FYI: I dug into exporter logs for one of the nodes; I see these sequences: `dcgm_exporter: collected ecc=1 xid=0` then `ecc=0 xid=1` within the same scrape. Might be exporter i/o ordering. I'll file an issue with vendor driver and attach logs.

matt: action items then: 1) I'll open PR to replace current per-event alerts with the sum-by rule (link posted when ready). 2) Sara — add a warning-level rule + dashboard panel for ephemeral spikes. 3) Lee — vendor/driver issue + sample logs. 4) Devops — review for label cardinality and perf.

maya: ping me on PR review for severity tuning. happy to help calibrate thresholds based on recent telemetry.

matt: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4387 — contains rule changes and test alerts in staging. please review. :eyes: 

devops: quick note — staging Prometheus currently has lower scrape interval; test in staging with prod-like scrape rates before rollout.

sara: scheduled a 30m calibration session tomorrow 10:00am PT to pick sensible thresholds and run the synthetic-noise job. invite sent.

matt: thanks all. dropping the current noisy per-sample pager in favor of the new rule after we validate in staging. will update runbook with the new triage steps. :thumbsup:
